acceptance: The codex reviewer jobs run read-only shell commands successfully in CI (for example by allowing unprivileged user namespaces for bubblewrap on the runner) without widening the sandbox beyond read-only
A shadow run shows a Codex reviewer reading a changed file (command_execution events with exit code 0) and returning a complete verdict
Until then, docs/operations/oracle-review-v2.md says Codex reviewers cannot read files in CI
context: Fixed in #2800 (merged 2026-10-09 11:16 UTC, e7eb5ce7e). Each Codex job runs `sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0` before the reviewer. A probe on a hosted runner (run 37881263281) reproduced "bwrap: loopback: Failed RTM_NEWADDR: Operation not permitted" with the setting at 1, and the sandboxed read worked at 0. Verified live in shadow run 37923401477 on canary #2803 (file-list brief, low-medium): luna returned a complete verdict after examining 10 files, and its SHIP WITH FIXES finding was real (the extra answer file breaks the qualification inventory and the answer-count assertion). The canary was closed and its branch deleted.
description: In shadow run 37861958813 (#2792, head afcf263b3) luna reported status incomplete: "The read-only shell commands needed to inspect the checkout failed before running: bwrap could not set up loopback (Operation not permitted)". `codex exec --sandbox read-only` on the GitHub-hosted runner cannot start its bubblewrap sandbox, likely because Ubuntu 24.04 restricts unprivileged user namespaces through AppArmor. So sol and luna can never read files in CI. This explains the earlier hollow Codex successes on file-list briefs, before verdict v2 made the reviewer report incomplete. Under the new protocol the absence is honest and the chain falls through, but the very-high chain is [opus, sol], so sol never contributes and opus is the only working very-high reviewer.
